distractors.reason: 'Hardly' means 'almost not' or 'barely'. 'Work hardly' suggests the opposite of the intended meaning.
'Heavily' is used with things like rain, smoke or drinking. We don't say 'work heavily'.
'Strongly' describes force or belief, as in 'strongly agree'. It is not used with 'work' in this sense.

example_sentence: You need to work ___ if you want to pass the exam.
l1_interference: Türkçede zarf genellikle fiilin önüne gelir, bu yüzden öğrenciler 'work hard' kalıbını kurarken zarfı fiilden önce koymaya ya da 'hard work' gibi isim yapısını fiil yerine kullanmaya eğilimlidir.
explanation: In English, adverbs of manner usually come after the verb, not before it. 'Hard' here means with a lot of effort, so 'work hard' is the natural pair.

related_collocations.example: She can speak fluently in three languages.
Please listen carefully to the instructions.
I didn't sleep well last night.

memory_tip: WORK HARD = put in a lot of effort | HARDLY = almost not (opposite meaning)
